paras: Look at the full Moon, and you will see the same dark patches your great-grandparents saw. In Chinese stories, they form a jade rabbit pounding medicine; in the West, people see a face, the Man in the Moon. Poets thousands of years ago saw exactly the same picture. The Moon always keeps one face toward Earth, and its other side stays hidden. Why?

It is not because the Moon does not spin. The Moon does rotate, exactly once each time it goes around Earth, about every 27.3 days. Try it yourself: walk in a circle around a chair while always facing the chair. When you get back to where you started, you have also turned around once, facing every wall of the room. The Moon does the same dance, so its near side always faces us.

Why are the two times exactly the same? The answer is tides. Earth's gravity stretches the Moon slightly, just as the Moon raises tides on Earth. Long ago, the young Moon spun faster. Earth kept tugging on its stretched shape like a brake, slowing the spin down until the bulge pointed straight at Earth and the Moon was locked in step. Most of the large moons in the solar system are locked to their planets in the same way.

The lock is not perfect. The Moon's orbit is a slight oval, so it moves faster when it is closer to Earth and slower when it is farther away, while its spin stays steady. Its spin axis is also tilted a little. As a result, the Moon seems to rock from side to side and nod up and down every month, letting us peek around its edges. Over time, we can see about 59 percent of its surface.

No one saw the far side until 1959, when the Soviet spacecraft Luna 3 photographed it. People sometimes call it the dark side, but it gets just as much sunlight as the near side; at new Moon, the far side is fully lit. In 2019, China's Chang'e 4 made the first landing on the far side and sent out a rover named Yutu-2, or Jade Rabbit 2. In 2024, Chang'e 6 brought back the first rocks from the far side.

The same face has looked down on all of human history. More than 2,000 years ago, the poet Qu Yuan asked why a rabbit sits in the Moon's belly. Tides are still at work today: they push the Moon about 3.8 centimeters farther away each year and slow down Earth's spin, making our day longer by about two thousandths of a second every hundred years. Look below to see how the real Moon is tipped today, and watch it rock over the coming weeks.
paras_zh: 看看滿月，你會看到和曾祖父母看過的一模一樣的暗色斑紋。在中國的故事裡，它們是一隻正在搗藥的玉兔；在西方，人們看到一張臉，叫「月亮上的人」。幾千年前的詩人看到的，也是同一幅圖。月亮永遠用同一面朝向地球，另一面一直藏著。為什麼？
不是因為月亮不自轉。月亮確實會自轉，而且每繞地球一圈，正好自轉一圈，大約 27.3 天。自己試試看：繞著一張椅子走一圈，臉一直朝著椅子。回到起點時，你也轉了一整圈，面對過房間的每一面牆。月亮跳的就是這支舞，所以它的正面永遠朝著我們。
為什麼兩個時間剛好一樣？答案是潮汐。地球的引力把月亮微微拉長，就像月亮在地球上造成潮汐一樣。很久以前，年輕的月亮轉得比較快。地球不斷拉著它被拉長的部分，像煞車一樣讓它越轉越慢，直到那個鼓起正對著地球，月亮就被「鎖」住了。太陽系裡大部分的大衛星，都用同樣的方式被它們的行星鎖住。
這把鎖並不完美。月亮的軌道是稍扁的橢圓，離地球近時走得快、遠時走得慢，自轉卻一直等速；它的自轉軸也有一點傾斜。結果月亮每個月好像左右搖一搖、上下點點頭，讓我們從邊緣偷看到一點點背面。日積月累，我們看得到月面的大約 59%。
直到 1959 年，蘇聯的太空船月球三號拍下照片，人類才第一次看見月球背面。有人叫它「暗面」，但它照到的陽光和正面一樣多；新月的時候，背面整個是亮的。2019 年，中國的嫦娥四號第一次在月球背面著陸，放出一輛叫「玉兔二號」的月球車。2024 年，嫦娥六號第一次從月球背面帶回岩石。
同一張臉，看著人類的全部歷史。兩千多年前，詩人屈原就在〈天問〉裡問：月亮的肚子裡為什麼有一隻兔子？潮汐到今天仍在作用：它每年把月亮推遠大約 3.8 公分，也讓地球越轉越慢，每一百年白天大約變長千分之二秒。看看下面今天真實的月亮微微轉向哪裡，接下來幾週再觀察它怎麼搖。
questions: Does the Moon spin? How long does one spin take?
What slowed down the Moon's spin long ago?
Why can we see about 59 percent of the Moon's surface instead of just half?
answers: Yes. It spins once every 27.3 days, exactly the time it takes to go around Earth once.
Tides: Earth's gravity tugged on the Moon's stretched shape like a brake until its spin matched its trip around Earth.
Because the Moon seems to rock and nod each month. Its orbit is an oval, so its speed changes while its spin stays steady, and its spin axis is a little tilted, so we can peek around its edges.

culture_cards.lead_en: Because the Moon never turns away, every culture has looked at the same patterns and told stories about them.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 因為月亮從不轉身，每個文化看到的都是同一組花紋，也各自說出了故事。

cards.en: A Rabbit in the Moon's Belly
cards.quote_zh: 夜光何德，死則又育？厥利維何，而顧菟在腹？——屈原〈天問〉
cards.quote_en: "What power has the night light, to die and then be born again? What good does it gain, with a rabbit in its belly?" (Qu Yuan, Heavenly Questions)
cards.body_en: More than 2,000 years ago, Qu Yuan asked about the waxing and waning Moon and the rabbit people saw in it. We still see that same rabbit, because the same face still looks at us.
cards.body_zh: 兩千多年前，屈原問月亮為什麼會圓缺，又問月中那隻兔子。我們今天看到的還是同一隻兔子，因為月亮還是同一張臉朝著我們。

cards.en: A Jade Rabbit on the Far Side
cards.body_en: China named its Moon program after Chang'e, the lady in the Moon, and its rovers after her jade rabbit. In 2019, Yutu-2 became the first rover to drive on the far side, where the rabbit's face can never be seen.
cards.body_zh: 中國的探月計畫以月中仙子嫦娥命名，月球車則叫「玉兔」。2019 年，玉兔二號成為第一輛在月球背面行駛的月球車——那裡正好是永遠看不到兔子的一面。

cards.en: The First Look Around the Back
cards.body_en: In October 1959, the Soviet spacecraft Luna 3 swung behind the Moon and photographed the far side. In 1968, the three astronauts of Apollo 8 became the first people to see it with their own eyes.
cards.body_zh: 1959 年 10 月，蘇聯的月球三號繞到月球後方，拍下背面的照片。1968 年，阿波羅 8 號的三位太空人成為第一批親眼看到月球背面的人。

cards.body_en: Far from the Sun, Pluto and its large moon Charon are locked to each other: each always shows the other the same face. Earth's spin is also slowing, but it would take far longer than the Sun will last for Earth to lock to the Moon.
cards.body_zh: 在遙遠的外太陽系，冥王星和它的大衛星凱倫互相鎖住：兩邊永遠用同一面對著彼此。地球的自轉也在變慢，但要慢到被月亮鎖住，所需的時間遠比太陽的壽命還長。

myths.myth_en: The Moon does not spin.
myths.myth_zh: 月亮不會自轉。
myths.fact_en: It spins once every 27.3 days, exactly as long as one trip around Earth. If it did not spin at all, we would see every side of it during a month.
myths.fact_zh: 它每 27.3 天自轉一圈，和繞地球一圈一樣久。如果完全不自轉，一個月裡我們反而會看到它的每一面。

myths.myth_en: The far side of the Moon is always dark.
myths.myth_zh: 月球背面永遠是暗的。
myths.fact_en: The far side gets just as much sunlight as the near side. At new Moon, when the side facing us is dark, the far side is fully lit. It is far, not dark.
myths.fact_zh: 背面照到的陽光和正面一樣多。新月時，朝著我們的一面是暗的，背面卻整個亮著。它是「遠」，不是「暗」。

myths.myth_en: We see exactly half of the Moon.
myths.myth_zh: 我們剛好看得到半個月亮。
myths.fact_en: Because the Moon rocks and nods a little each month, we can see about 59 percent of its surface over time.
myths.fact_zh: 因為月亮每個月會微微搖晃、點頭，日積月累我們看得到大約 59% 的月面。

myths.myth_en: The Moon has always shown us the same face.
myths.myth_zh: 月亮從一開始就用同一面對著我們。
myths.fact_en: The young Moon spun faster. Tides from Earth slowed it down until it became locked, long before there were people to watch.
myths.fact_zh: 年輕的月亮轉得比較快，是地球的潮汐讓它慢下來、最後被鎖住——那是遠在人類出現之前的事。

materials.en: A chair to be Earth, in the middle of an open space
materials.zh: 一張椅子當地球，放在空地中央

materials.en: A paper plate with a face drawn on it, held in front of the walker's chest (the Moon's near side)
materials.zh: 一個畫了臉的紙盤，拿在走路的人胸前（月亮的正面）

materials.en: Signs on the four walls: North, East, South, West
materials.zh: 四面牆貼上「北、東、南、西」

steps.en: One student walks slowly in a circle around the chair, always keeping the plate's face toward the chair.
steps.zh: 一位同學慢慢繞著椅子走一圈，紙盤上的臉一直朝著椅子。

steps.en: The class calls out which wall sign the walker's back is facing. Did it change? (Yes: the walker turned once.)
steps.zh: 全班喊出走路的人背後對著哪一面牆。有變嗎？（有：走路的人轉了一圈。）

steps.en: Now walk around again, but keep facing the North wall the whole time. What does the chair see? (The back of the plate.)
steps.zh: 再走一圈，但這次一直面向北牆。椅子看到什麼？（紙盤的背面。）

steps.en: Discuss: which walk is like the real Moon?
steps.zh: 討論：哪一種走法像真實的月亮？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: then switch the 3D model between Real Moon and No spin, and compare it with the two walks.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：接著把 3D 模型在「真實」和「不自轉」之間切換，和兩種走法對照。

steps.en: Find Mare Crisium, the round dark patch near the Moon's right edge, on the page's picture.
steps.zh: 在頁面的月亮圖上找到危海：靠近右邊緣的一塊圓形暗斑。

steps.zh: 兩週內挑幾個晚上，在圓圈裡畫出危海的位置，寫上日期。

steps.zh: 對照頁面：那幾天是不是東緣轉過來的日子？

activities.tip_en: Tip: Mare Crisium is on the side lit by a waxing Moon in the evening, so the first two weeks after new Moon work best.
activities.tip_zh: 提示：危海在傍晚的盈月亮面上，所以新月後的頭兩週最好觀察。

lessons.title: What Is the Milky Way?
lessons.blurb_en: The glowing band across a dark summer sky is our own galaxy, seen from the inside. Fly out of the disk, then back to the Sun's place, and find where the band lies over Changhua tonight.
lessons.blurb_zh: 暗夜裡橫過天空的那條光帶，是我們從「裡面」看到的自己的星系。飛出星系盤，再回到太陽的位置，找找今晚彰化天上的銀河在哪裡。
lessons.big_idea_en: The Milky Way is our galaxy, a flat disk of hundreds of billions of stars. We live inside the disk, so when we look along it, the light of countless distant stars blends into a glowing band across the sky.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 銀河就是我們所在的星系：一個由幾千億顆恆星組成的扁平圓盤。我們住在盤子裡面，順著盤面看出去，無數遙遠星星的光融成一條橫過天空的光帶。

lab.title_zh: 住在一個扁平的圓盤裡
lab.how_en: Start outside the galaxy and find the Sun, marked in gold, out in the disk. Switch to Edge-on to see how flat the disk is. Then choose From the Sun: now you are inside the disk, and the stars along it pile up into a band that circles you, brightest toward the center in Sagittarius. The real bright stars are drawn around you, with Altair and Vega on opposite banks. On the right, the band is drawn over the real sky above Changhua.
lab.how_zh: 先從星系外面找到太陽（金色記號），它在盤面靠外的地方。切換到「側面看」，看看這個盤子有多扁。再選「從太陽看」：現在你在盤子裡面，沿著盤面的星星疊成一條繞著你一圈的光帶，往人馬座的銀河中心最亮；周圍也畫上了真實的亮星，牛郎星和織女星正好在光帶兩岸。右邊把銀河畫在彰化真實的星空上。

legend.en: Gold ring: the Sun, about 26,000 light-years from the center
legend.zh: 金色圈：太陽，離中心約 2.6 萬光年

legend.en: Blue-white: young stars in the spiral arms; yellow: older stars in the bulge and bar
legend.zh: 藍白色：旋臂裡的年輕恆星；黃色：核球與棒裡的老恆星

legend.en: Right chart: the Milky Way band over Changhua, from real galactic coordinates
legend.zh: 右側星圖：彰化天上的銀河光帶，照真實銀道座標畫

legend.en: One unit is 1,000 light-years; the whole disk is about 100,000 light-years across
legend.zh: 1 單位＝1,000 光年；整個盤面寬約 10 萬光年

lab.scale_en: The galaxy here is a drawing based on what astronomers know: its size, thickness, bar, spiral arms, and the Sun's place. No one has ever photographed our galaxy from outside. The directions in the From the Sun view and the band on the sky chart use real galactic coordinates, and the stars are real.
lab.scale_zh: 這裡的銀河是依天文學家已知的大小、厚度、棒狀結構、旋臂與太陽位置畫出來的示意圖——從來沒有人從外面拍過我們的星系。「從太陽看」的方向與星圖上的光帶用的是真實銀道座標，星星也是真的。
lab.credit_html:

銀道座標：國際天文聯合會（IAU）定義（J2000）。到銀心的距離：GRAVITY 合作團隊（2019）。星表：耶魯亮星星表第五版（公有領域）。銀河本身是繪製的模型。

paras: Far from city lights, on a clear summer night, a pale, glowing band stretches across the sky like a river of mist. In Chinese, it is called the Silver River or the River of Heaven; in English, it is the Milky Way. For thousands of years, people wondered what it was. Was it a cloud? A road across the sky? A river of milk?

In 1610, Galileo turned one of the first telescopes toward it and saw that the band is made of countless faint stars, too far away and too close together for our eyes to tell apart. Today we know that the Milky Way is our galaxy: a huge, flat disk of hundreds of billions of stars, along with gas and dust, all held together by gravity. Our Sun is just one of those stars.

So why does it look like a band? We live inside the disk, about 26,000 light-years from its center. When we look along the disk, our view passes through enormous numbers of stars, and their light blends into a glowing band. When we look up or down, out of the disk, we see far fewer. Imagine standing in a crowd spread out across a wide, flat field: look straight ahead and you see people all around you, but look up and you see only sky.

The disk is about 100,000 light-years across but only about 1,000 light-years thick, flatter than a pancake. At its center is a bulge of older stars and a black hole about four million times as heavy as the Sun. Spiral arms wind out from the center, and the whole galaxy turns. The Sun takes about 230 million years to go around once. The last time it was where it is now, the first dinosaurs were appearing.

In Chinese stories, the Milky Way is the river that keeps the Cowherd and the Weaver Girl apart. Look for them in the evening sky: Altair and Vega shine on opposite banks of the band. The ancient Book of Songs describes the bright River of Clouds turning across the sky. The Greeks said it was milk spilled by the goddess Hera, and that is why our word galaxy comes from the Greek word for milk.

Sadly, more than a third of the people on Earth can no longer see the Milky Way from home, because city lights hide it. In Taiwan, the best time to see its bright center is a summer evening, from a dark place such as the Hehuan Mountain Dark Sky Park. Use the chart below to find where the band lies over Changhua tonight.
paras_zh: 遠離城市燈光的晴朗夏夜，一條淡淡發光的帶子橫過天空，像一條霧氣做的河。中文叫它「銀河」或「天河」，英文叫 Milky Way（牛奶路）。幾千年來，人們一直在想它是什麼：一片雲？一條橫過天空的路？還是一條牛奶河？
1610 年，伽利略把最早的望遠鏡之一對準它，發現這條光帶是由無數暗淡的星星組成的——它們太遠、又擠得太近，眼睛分不開。今天我們知道，銀河就是我們所在的星系：一個由幾千億顆恆星，加上氣體和塵埃，靠引力聚在一起的巨大扁平圓盤。我們的太陽只是其中一顆。
那它為什麼看起來是一條帶子？因為我們住在盤子裡面，離中心大約 2.6 萬光年。順著盤面看出去，視線穿過數不清的星星，它們的光融成一條發光的帶子；往盤面上下看，星星就少多了。想像你站在一大片平坦的空地上，四周散滿了人：平視時四面八方都是人，往上看卻只有天空。
這個盤子寬約 10 萬光年，厚度卻只有約 1,000 光年，比煎餅還扁。中心是一團由老恆星組成的核球，還有一個質量約太陽 400 萬倍的黑洞。旋臂從中心盤旋而出，整個星系都在轉。太陽繞一圈大約要 2.3 億年；上一次它在現在這個位置時，最早的恐龍才剛出現。
在中國的故事裡，銀河是隔開牛郎和織女的那條河。傍晚找找看：牛郎星和織女星正好在光帶的兩岸。古老的《詩經》寫過明亮的「雲漢」在天上流轉；希臘人則說它是天后赫拉灑出的乳汁，所以英文的 galaxy（星系）來自希臘文的「乳汁」。
可惜的是，地球上超過三分之一的人，在家已經看不到銀河了，因為城市燈光把它遮住了。在台灣，看明亮的銀河中心最好的時間是夏天傍晚，地點要夠暗，例如合歡山暗空公園。用下面的星圖找找看，今晚彰化天上的銀河在哪裡。

culture_cards.lead_en: East and West, people saw the Milky Way as a river, a road, or a stream of milk, long before anyone knew it was made of stars.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 在知道它是由星星組成之前很久，東西方的人就把銀河看成一條河、一條路，或一道乳汁。

cards.quote_zh: 倬彼雲漢，昭回于天。——《詩經．大雅．雲漢》
cards.quote_en: "Bright is that River of Clouds, shining and turning across the sky." (Book of Songs)
cards.body_en: In this ancient poem, a king looks up at the Milky Way during a terrible drought and prays for rain. Chinese has many names for it: the River of Clouds, the River of Heaven, and the Silver River.
cards.body_zh: 這首古詩裡，一位君王在大旱時仰望銀河、祈求降雨。中文替銀河取了很多名字：雲漢、天河、河漢、銀漢、銀河。

cards.quote_zh: 纖雲弄巧，飛星傳恨，銀漢迢迢暗度。——秦觀〈鵲橋仙〉
cards.quote_en: "Thin clouds weave their art, shooting stars carry sorrow, and far across the Silver River she quietly crosses." (Qin Guan)
cards.body_en: On the night of Qixi, the Weaver Girl crosses the Milky Way to meet the Cowherd. In the sky, Vega and Altair really do sit on opposite sides of the band, about 15 light-years apart (Lesson 10).
cards.body_zh: 七夕夜，織女渡過銀河與牛郎相會。在天上，織女星和牛郎星真的分在銀河兩岸，相距約 15 光年（第十課）。

cards.body_en: The ancient Greeks called it the milky circle and told of milk spilled by the goddess Hera. The Latin name became the Milky Way, and the Greek word for milk, gala, gave us the word galaxy.
cards.body_zh: 古希臘人叫它「乳白色的圓環」，說是天后赫拉灑出的乳汁。拉丁文變成英文的 Milky Way，而希臘文的「乳汁」（gala）就是英文 galaxy（星系）的字源。

cards.body_en: Galileo first saw that the Milky Way is made of stars. Later astronomers thought the Sun sat near the middle, until Harlow Shapley showed in 1918, using star clusters, that the center lies far away in the direction of Sagittarius.
cards.body_zh: 伽利略第一個看出銀河是由星星組成。後來的天文學家以為太陽在銀河正中央，直到 1918 年，沙普利用星團證明銀河中心其實遠在人馬座方向。

myths.myth_en: The Milky Way is a cloud in our sky.
myths.myth_zh: 銀河是天上的一片雲。
myths.fact_en: It is the light of countless stars thousands of light-years away, too faint and crowded for our eyes to see one by one.
myths.fact_zh: 它是幾千光年外數不清的星星發出的光，太暗又太擠，眼睛分不出一顆一顆。

myths.myth_en: Pictures of a spiral galaxy show our Milky Way from outside.
myths.myth_zh: 那些漩渦星系的圖片，是從外面拍的銀河。
myths.fact_en: No spacecraft has ever left our galaxy. Pictures of the Milky Way from outside are drawings based on measurements, or photos of other galaxies.
myths.fact_zh: 沒有任何太空船離開過銀河。從外面看的銀河圖，不是依測量資料畫的示意圖，就是其他星系的照片。

myths.myth_en: The Sun is at the center of the galaxy.
myths.myth_zh: 太陽在銀河的中心。
myths.fact_en: The Sun is about 26,000 light-years from the center, roughly halfway out. The center lies in the direction of Sagittarius.
myths.fact_zh: 太陽離中心約 2.6 萬光年，大約在一半的地方。銀河中心在人馬座的方向。

myths.myth_en: Only the stars in the band belong to the Milky Way.
myths.myth_zh: 只有光帶裡的星星屬於銀河。
myths.fact_en: Every star you can see without a telescope belongs to our galaxy. They are just our nearer neighbors, scattered all around us. The Andromeda Galaxy, 2.5 million light-years away, is one of the very few other galaxies visible to the eye.
myths.fact_zh: 肉眼看得到的每一顆星都屬於銀河，只是比較近、散在我們周圍。250 萬光年外的仙女座星系，是極少數肉眼看得到的其他星系之一。

tricks.body_en: We live inside a flat disk of stars, so we see it edge-on, as a band.
tricks.body_zh: 我們住在扁平的星盤裡，從側面看出去，就是一條帶子。

tricks.body_en: The disk is about 100,000 light-years wide and 1,000 light-years thick.
tricks.body_zh: 盤面寬約 10 萬光年，厚約 1,000 光年。

tricks.body_en: Altair and Vega shine on opposite sides of the Milky Way.
tricks.body_zh: 牛郎星和織女星分在銀河兩岸。

tricks.body_en: The bright center is up on summer evenings; in winter we look toward the faint outer edge.
tricks.body_zh: 夏天傍晚看得到明亮的銀心；冬天看的是比較淡的外緣。

materials.en: The whole class and a playground
materials.zh: 全班同學和一片操場

materials.en: Chalk to mark a large circle
materials.zh: 粉筆，畫一個大圓圈

materials.en: A hat or sign for the student who plays the Sun
materials.zh: 一頂帽子或牌子，給扮演太陽的同學

steps.en: Draw a large circle. Everyone stands inside it, spread out but more crowded near the middle: this is the galaxy's disk.
steps.zh: 畫一個大圓。全班站在圈裡，分散開來，但越靠中間越擠：這就是銀河的盤面。

steps.en: One student, the Sun, stands about halfway between the middle and the edge.
steps.zh: 一位同學扮太陽，站在中心到邊緣大約一半的地方。

steps.en: The Sun turns slowly and looks straight ahead: classmates fill the view all the way around, most toward the middle.
steps.zh: 太陽慢慢轉一圈、平視前方：四周都是同學，往中心的方向最多。

steps.en: Now the Sun looks up: only sky. Discuss: how is this like the Milky Way band?
steps.zh: 再往上看：只有天空。討論：這和天上的銀河光帶有什麼像的地方？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: then open the 3D model and switch from Outside to From the Sun.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：接著打開 3D 模型，從「從外面看」切換到「從太陽看」。

materials.en: The sky chart on this page, to find the Summer Triangle (Vega, Altair, and Deneb)
materials.zh: 本頁的星圖，用來找夏季大三角（織女星、牛郎星、天津四）

materials.en: A red flashlight and a worksheet
materials.zh: 一支紅光手電筒和一張學習單

materials.en: An adult to come along
materials.zh: 一位大人陪同

steps.en: On a clear, moonless evening, find the Summer Triangle from your home or school.
steps.zh: 在晴朗、沒有月亮的傍晚，從家裡或學校找到夏季大三角。

steps.en: Let your eyes adjust for 15 minutes, then count how many stars you can see inside the triangle.
steps.zh: 讓眼睛適應 15 分鐘，數數三角形裡看得到幾顆星。

steps.en: If you can, count again from a darker place, such as the countryside or a mountain.
steps.zh: 有機會的話，到更暗的地方（鄉下或山上）再數一次。

steps.en: Compare the class's results. Where could you see the Milky Way running through the triangle?
steps.zh: 比較全班的結果：在哪些地方看得到銀河穿過三角形？
